comments.author: Chao Huang
comments.comment:
Most agent frameworks focus on orchestrating a single LLM. What changes when you treat each agent as a specialized tool and route tasks between them?

I've found the hard part isn't the router logic—it's building a shared state layer that all agents can reliably read and write to without conflicts. This is where most multi-agent systems break in production.

What's your biggest challenge when trying to get multiple AI agents to collaborate?

comments.author: Prasanth N.
comments.comment: Most teams miss that a 10% model performance gain can be eaten by a 20% increase in orchestration latency. How do you measure your system's total cost of intelligence, not just model calls?

comments.author: Miles Teller
comments.comment:
Most agent frameworks treat "reasoning" as a single step. In practice, I've found a high-performing loop often splits it: a fast, cheap LLM for planning the next action, and a more capable, expensive one for verifying the output before execution. This cuts costs without sacrificing reliability.

What's your most effective tweak to the standard ReAct loop?
